text: If some straight-line touches a circle, and some (other) straight-line is joined from the center (of the circle) to the point of contact, (then) the (straight-line) so joined will be perpendicular to the tangent. For let some straight-line $DE$ touch the circle $ABC$ at point $C$, and let the center $F$ of circle $ABC$ be found [Prop.~3.1], and let $FC$ be joined from $F$ to $C$. I say that $FC$ is perpendicular to $DE$.
For if not, let $FG$ be drawn from $F$, perpendicular to $DE$ [Prop.~1.12].
assertion: FG is drawn from F, perpendicular to DE

text: Therefore, since angle $FGC$ is a right-angle, (angle) $FCG$ is thus acute [Prop.~1.17].
And the greater angle is subtended by the greater side [Prop.~1.19]. Thus, $FC$ (is) greater than $FG$.

text: Thus, $FB$ (is) also greater than $FG$, the lesser than the greater.

assertion: FG is not perpendicular to DE

text: So, similarly, we can show that neither (is) any other (straight-line) except $FC$.
assertion: no other straight-line (except FC) is perpendicular to DE

text: Thus, if some straight-line touches a circle, and some (other) straight-line is joined from the center (of the circle) to the point of contact, (then) the (straight-line) so joined will be perpendicular to the tangent. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
